html:
The Sahtú Got'ine, "the people of Great Bear Lake", are a Dene people of Great Bear Lake in the Northwest Territories, Canada. Their main community is Délı̨nę, on the lake's southwest shore. They speak North Slavey, an Athabaskan language, and fished the lake and hunted caribou.

In the 1930s pitchblende was found at Port Radium on the lake's east shore. Délı̨nę men were hired to carry sacks of uranium ore, some of which went into the bombs of the Manhattan Project. Many later died of cancer, and Délı̨nę came to be called the "village of widows". The Sahtú signed Treaty 11 in 1921, and the Sahtu Dene and Metis land claim agreement in 1993. In 2016 Délı̨nę became the first community in the Northwest Territories to govern itself under its own self-government agreement. Their neighbours are the Tłı̨chǫ to the south and the Dehcho Dene up the Mackenzie.
